briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 23, 2026.

sections.title: 🚨 Worsening Extreme Weather Phenomena and Societal Impacts
sections.content: Today's climate-related news warns of the severe impacts that unprecedented extreme weather phenomena are having on our society. Alongside the pessimistic outlook that this year may be recorded as the coolest year, future heatwaves reaching 45 degrees Celsius, and more powerful torrential rains and typhoons are anticipated [9]. Seoul, for instance, experienced 12 consecutive nights of tropical heat and humid sweltering conditions with a perceived temperature of 33 degrees Celsius, leading to the issuance of a heatwave advisory [44]. The phenomenon of increasing heavy rainfall and drought disasters, despite similar annual precipitation, demonstrates that climate change is drastically altering precipitation patterns [4]. A drier Earth is also linked to the unexpected spread of infectious diseases [10], and analysis suggests that heatwaves and extreme weather can even disrupt the social connections people rely on, potentially making us feel more isolated [47].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Climate Crisis and Adaptation Efforts in the Agricultural Sector
sections.content: Climate change poses a direct threat to the domestic agricultural sector, with a particular emergency in high-altitude cabbage cultivation, prompting the Rural Development Administration to seek heat and disease-resistant varieties [1]. Amidst this crisis, Gyeongsangbuk-do Province is actively disseminating melon cultivation techniques to farms to protect crops against abnormal climate conditions, especially high temperatures [7, 8]. Internationally, changes in cultivation environments due to climate change are evident, such as the grape harvest season in Croatia shifting earlier to August [49]. Meanwhile, the emergence of 'WISE,' a K-agriculture digital platform that predicts global droughts and floods, underscores the importance of precision agriculture in responding to climate change [12].

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Community-Led Carbon Neutrality Practices
sections.content: On a positive note, community-led carbon neutrality efforts are expanding across the nation. Daejeon's Daedeok-gu is actively promoting carbon-neutral practices tailored to local characteristics in areas like Deogam-dong and Jungni-dong [15, 16]. Gwangmyeong-si and Pocheon-si are also adopting carbon neutrality initiatives through resident assemblies and resident self-governance council agreements [13, 19, 20, 24]. Encouragement for action through education and play is also notable, such as ecological exploration education seeking climate crisis solutions in the DMZ forest [6, 22] and a carbon-neutral escape room game utilizing 'Yumi's Cells' characters [21]. The cultural and arts sector is also participating in carbon neutrality with a 5-minute lights-out campaign [23], and various stakeholders, including Kunsan National University sharing carbon neutrality internship achievements, are leading the way in carbon-neutral practices [25].

sections.title: ⚠️ Dilemmas and Opportunities in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a core task for achieving carbon neutrality, yet it faces several dilemmas. Particularly in China, a perplexing paradox is occurring where diligently expanded renewable energy, equivalent to Mexico's annual electricity consumption, is being wasted due to grid issues [31, 35, 42]. This highlights the severity of grid congestion, a problem for which the International Energy Agency (IEA) has warned of the need for 67 trillion KRW in investment [32]. Domestically, the uncertainty of renewable energy and the prolonged construction of nuclear power plants are exacerbating the LNG dilemma in achieving the government's carbon reduction targets [30, 43]. Furthermore, concerns are being raised that the advancement of the AI industry could accelerate greenhouse gas emissions [2]. Nevertheless, Saemangeum is emerging as a hub for future high-tech industries, including AI, robotics, hydrogen, and renewable energy [28]. Local governments and businesses in areas like Pyeongtaek and Jeonju are making multifaceted efforts, exploring solutions for renewable energy transition, discussing solar power utilization, and considering energy citizen income [29, 33, 34, 36, 38, 41].

sections.title: 🌍 Voices on Climate Policy and International Response
sections.content: As awareness of the reality of climate change grows, so too do calls for policy responses. Following extreme heatwaves, Busan City is pursuing climate insurance for its citizens, seeking to establish a social safety net against climate disasters [3]. Internationally, there is also a critical perspective on the situation where, despite the clear reality of climate change, action is still not being sufficiently urged [48]. In some regions, such as Puerto Rico, comments suggest that governments are facing situations where they cannot supply water to citizens due to climate change, indicating a deepening impact of the climate crisis on social infrastructure and administrative capacity [46]. These circumstances underscore the urgent need for stronger and more immediate action from governments and the international community to address climate change.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severity of extreme weather phenomena and the complex challenges of the renewable energy transition, while also demonstrating that hope can be found in community-led carbon neutrality efforts and adaptation attempts in the agricultural sector. Comprehensive and integrated efforts are urgently needed to address the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
